title: Who Won Every Season of ‘America’s Got Talent’?
summary: Here's a complete list of which talented act won at the end of every AGT season.
body: NBC’s America’s Got Talent is one of the country’s leading talent competition shows, and Billboard is looking back at the many gifted winners who’ve made history on the series so far. Created by former American Idol judge, X Factor mastermind and Syco Entertainment founder Simon Cowell , the global talent competition premiered in the U.S. on NBC in 2006. The idea was to find the best talent of any age in the country — whether they specialized in singing, dancing, performing magic tricks, acting as a ventriloquist or even training dogs to do tricks — and then have them headline a show on the Las Vegas Strip on top of winning a $1 million cash prize. The show has seen a number of stars grace its judges’ panel, with the just-wrapped season 21 featuring Cowell alongside Mel B , Sofia Vergara and Howie Mandel , as well as host Terry Crews . Each of the judges recruits viewers’ votes to help crown the most talented contestant, and each season’s top pick runs the gamut of skill sets. A handful of musicians have come out on top in the past, including the show’s first-ever champ, then-11-year-old singer Bianca Ryan , whose tiny frame belied her massive pipes on the …

title: Pixel users report Bluetooth volume control issues with Android 17 QPR1
summary: Absolute volume is busted for some.
body: TL;DR Multiple users report that absolute volume is no longer working the way it used to on their Pixel devices as of Android 17 QPR1. We don’t know what’s causing this issue or whether a fix is in the works. As is often the case around significant OS updates, Pixel users have been reporting all kinds of issues since Android 17 QPR1 started rolling out. We’ve seen users complain about problems with performance, touch detection, reception, and then some. Today, we’ve seen some reports that Pixel owners are having trouble with volume control. Reddit user KaneNova posted on the Google Pixel subreddit today saying that since downloading the September update on their Pixel 10, absolute volume, which syncs volume levels on Bluetooth headphones and the device they’re streaming audio from, has stopped working.

Chrome now preserves your scroll position and partially filled forms when you send tabs between devices. Studying back when I was still in school looked a lot different compared to what it’s like today . While the struggles back in the day involved ensuring you had all the information, students today face the opposite problem , and Google wants to help fix that. The sheer amount of information around topics available today can feel overwhelming, and finding and making sense of just the right information can be challenging. Google is introducing three new Chrome features aimed at making that process a tad bit easier.

title: Google Home error warns users of movement even when they’re at home
summary: Users are getting flooded with notifications.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google Home users have been getting inundated by motion sensor alerts. Reportedly, notifications are being sent even when users are at home. It appears the issue may have resolved itself. If you want to improve the security of your home, it makes sense to install motion sensors and enable alerts. That way, you’ll be notified if there is ever suspicious activity happening at your home while you’re away. At the same time, you don’t exactly need to be warned about detected movement while you’re at your abode. For some users, it appears that Google Home thinks differently. Google Home users are reporting that they are getting inundated with motion alert notifications. No, this isn’t a large-scale burglary operation that’s currently underway. Rather, Google Home is warning of detected movement while users are at their residences. Which means anytime they make a move, Google Home is sending them an alert.

title: Privacy Display on the Galaxy S27 Ultra could pick up this handy new trick
summary: Split-screen display dimming could make it to the early 2027 Samsung flagship.
body: TL;DR Prominent leaker Ice Universe claims the Galaxy S27 Ultra will introduce a split-screen Privacy Display feature, as seen on the Xiaomi 18 Pro series. This feature can cleverly dim just one app window in split-screen view, even when it’s resized. While Xiaomi appears to have more features tied to this privacy feature, the leaker notes that Samsung still has the upper hand in overall dimming capacity. Samsung set the industry standard by introducing Privacy Display on the Galaxy S26 Ultra , which enables hardware-level screen dimming to shake off shoulder surfers. While some brands have already revealed their own take on this feature, the freshly announced Xiaomi 18 Pro series takes it to another level with Smart Privacy Display. We’re now learning that Samsung may introduce at least one of the Xiaomi flagship’s privacy-oriented features in its early 2027 smartphone. Writing on X, leaker Ice Universe claims the Xiaomi 18 Pro’s unique split-screen privacy protection system will make its way to the Galaxy S27 Ultra . This split-screen privacy mechanism cleverly dims only one app, even as you resize it, while keeping the other in its normal, visible state.

summary: Dolphin's latest update brings Netplay online multiplayer to Android and cross-platform support so mobile and PC users.
body: TL;DR Dolphin Emulator finally supports NetPlay on Android. The update lets users play online multiplayer with GameCube and Wii titles. Dolphin’s latest update also extends NetPlay to cross-platform instances. Dolphin Emulator is unquestionably one of the most popular retro game emulators for Android, Windows, Mac, and even a Steam Deck. It’s the first option enthusiasts turn to for Nintendo Wii and GameCube because of its upscaling, custom graphics mods, and easy Bluetooth and USB controller support, among other features. Another advantage of Dolphin is that it lets you play games originally designed for local multiplayer online, enabled by a feature called NetPlay. Traditionally, this feature required a specific mechanism to sync gameplay across multiple devices and was therefore limited to scenarios where all players are on the same operating system—and to desktop environments. That changes now with Dolphin announcing NetPlay support for Android and opening it up for cross-platform gameplay. title: Google Messages has a camera flash problem, and nobody knows why
summary: Another day, another Google Messages bug.
body: TL;DR Multiple Google Messages users are having trouble with the timing of the LED flash when taking photos in chats. In some cases, the LED flash simply refuses to activate even when toggled manually, though it functions normally in other camera apps. The issue certainly isn’t new, with similar complaints emerging over a month ago. One common function of a messaging app is sending images and videos to the people you know. Apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Google Messages , along with several others, offer a camera interface in the chat to capture and send media. It now looks like Google’s messaging app may be stumbling at this basic function in some situations. A Verizon-branded Galaxy S24 Ultra owner on Reddit says Google Messages refuses to activate the flash while capturing an image from the chat. They note that the flash timing is off, meaning it triggers much before the photo is captured, resulting in a dark image.

title: Data privacy isn’t just for nerds — here’s why you should care too
summary: The more I see how my personal data is used across services, the more I want to guard my privacy.
body: A lot of times when I’ve mentioned moving to more privacy-focused apps and services, the reaction is more than a shrug — it’s a declaration that online privacy isn’t all that important. Most recently, at a tech event, I mentioned moving to Brave to avoid Google’s data collection and targeted advertising, and another attendee said that it’s just not important to them. That’s when I realized that there’s this general misunderstanding that prioritizing data privacy is the pastime of nerds and those prone to donning tin foil hats. I know I was someone who used to take a more laissez-faire approach to my online privacy. Years later, after grappling with the consequences of this, I feel that data privacy and data collection should be something everyone cares about.

title: GrapheneOS just confirmed its first supported non-Pixel phone
summary: GrapheneOS users are finally getting a serious alternative to Google’s Pixels.
body: TL;DR GrapheneOS has confirmed that the Motorola Signature 27 will be its first officially supported Motorola phone. The flagship fits GrapheneOS’s stated hardware requirements, including a top-end Snapdragon chip and long-term software support. The move gives GrapheneOS users a major alternative to Pixels as the project increasingly pushes beyond Google hardware and services. For years, wanting GrapheneOS meant accepting one hardware choice: you needed a Google Pixel. Motorola’s partnership with the privacy-focused project promised to break that lock-in, but until now, we didn’t know which phone would go first. Following this week’s Signature 27 unveiling , GrapheneOS has answered that question directly: Motorola’s new flagship will be the first phone supported under the partnership. The confirmation came after an X user asked whether the Signature 27 would support GrapheneOS. “Yes, that will be the initial supported phone. Wait for official news about it,” the project replied . That last sentence matters, since GrapheneOS has not yet announced when support will arrive or whether Motorola will offer the OS preinstalled.

title: Qualcomm is solving Snapdragon X’s Linux problem
summary: Bringing this powerful operating system to the very latest in mobile computing hardware.
body: TL;DR Qualcomm shares that Snapdragon X-series laptops are getting Linux support. Debian compatibility should roll out sometime later in 2026. Ubuntu is planning support for Snapdragon X2 devices early next year. It’s taken a couple decades, but something big has finally started happening for how we get computing done on laptops. After years of trying to be tiny desktop computers, running the same kind of chips that were never really designed for power efficiency, laptops began broadly embracing RISC computing — including models built around Qualcomm Snapdragon chips like the X series . This week at Qualcomm’s annual Snapdragon Summit, the company is sharing news of a big new upgrade for such models that power users are really going to love. For all the speed and battery life they offer, Snapdragon laptops have had at least one big blind spot: Linux. Even though different Snapdragon chips have been powering Android (with its deep Linux roots) devices for ages, initial Snapdragon X laptops lacked support for mainstream Linux distros .

title: Apple’s iPhone Duo could help fix one of Android’s biggest foldable problems
summary: More foldable users could finally give developers a reason to optimize.
body: TL;DR Google’s Android boss says growing interest in foldables could give developers more reason to optimize their apps for larger screens. Some Android apps still haven’t properly adapted to foldables, but Google says developers are either working on improvements or talking with the company. Apple’s iPhone Duo could expand the foldable audience enough to encourage better app experiences across both iOS and Android. Android foldables have spent years getting the hardware right, but the app problem has been much harder to shake. Apple’s arrival with the iPhone Duo could finally give developers another reason to take foldable layouts seriously, and Google’s Android boss thinks Android users could benefit too. Speaking to Tom’s Guide , Android Ecosystem President Sameer Samat said developers see more value in investing in foldables as the form factor becomes more popular. More importantly, he acknowledged that some apps still haven’t made that transition, adding that their developers are either working on it or already in conversations with Google. title: Blame this Google Maps Android Auto bug for your next speeding ticket

body: TL;DR Multiple users have reported that Google Maps’ speedometer is switching from MPH to KPH (or vice versa). The issue seems to primarily affect Android Auto, but at least one user reports a similar experience on the mobile app. It’s not currently clear why this is happening or how widespread the issue is. One of Google Maps’ useful features is that the app can show both the posted speed limit on the street where you’re driving and the speed you’re currently traveling, as calculated by GPS. This week, though, many users are reporting that Google Maps on Android Auto is bungling that feature in a strange way. In a Reddit thread (as spotted by Auto Evolution ), four users all say that the speedometer in Google Maps on Android Auto has started alternating between miles per hour and kilometers per hour, irrespective of their own settings. One user even says they’re experiencing the same issue in Google Maps on their phone.

body: TL;DR YouTube is turning its earlier Custom Feed experiment into a full feature that lets you build recommendation feeds with conversational prompts. You can save multiple feeds for different interests, moods, or routines, and YouTube will keep them updated with fresh recommendations. Custom Feeds are coming soon to users in the US across mobile, web, and TVs. YouTube’s Home tab has always had a funny way of overreacting. Watch one random woodworking video, and suddenly the algorithm can decide you’ve found your new life’s calling. Last year, YouTube started testing a way to fight that problem by letting some users tell an AI chatbot what they actually wanted to see. title: I’ve used Razr phones for 20 years, and Motorola’s secret weapon hasn’t changed
summary: Motorola understands who buys its phones.
body: I’ve used Motorola phones longer than I’d like to admit. The Nokia 5160 I carried around in high school will always hold a special place in my heart, but Motorola soon became my preferred brand. I remember how jealous I was when my parents bought StarTACs. It’s hard to describe what a shift that device was for cell phones. Moto proved that the phones in our pockets could be smaller and more stylish, and the company wasn’t done there. The original Razr was a revelation when it was released in 2004. You didn’t want to buy anything else at the time, and it was hard to go anywhere without seeing someone use one. It’s why Motorola’s recent success isn’t a surprise. The company has maintained a consistent theme over the last two decades, and it doesn’t take much to see where that all began and how it translates perfectly to this current crop of Razrs.

title: The Sleenova SoundMask fixed my biggest issue with sleep earbuds
summary: Speakers next to your ears instead of inside them is a big deal for a side sleeper like me.
body: I’ve tested a handful of sleep earbuds over the years, and no matter how small they get, I haven’t found a pair that doesn’t create pressure in my ears while sleeping on my side, which can be uncomfortable. The Sleenova SoundMask avoids that problem with speakers built into the sides of a sleep mask that sits next to your ears. After a few nights with it, it became a pretty reliable tool for getting a good night’s rest, with its own tradeoffs to sleep earbuds. No more sore ears The SoundMask is very comfortable. Rather than pressing flat against your eyelids, there’s a contoured cavity that lifts the fabric off your eyes entirely, so you can blink and move your eyes freely without anything rubbing against them. There is ample padding around the eyes and nose, so that I could sleep face-down into a pillow without discomfort. It also blocks out light surprisingly well. I couldn’t see anything while wearing it, even in a fully lit room.

title: Qualcomm could finally fix a major issue with PC emulation on Android
summary: Does this mean we won't have to download custom Turnip drivers anymore?
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Qualcomm reportedly plans to improve support for PC game emulation on Android devices via its official GPU drivers. The company is also apparently thinking about bringing DirectX12 support to its GPU drivers on Android. This could potentially result in better performance and improved compatibility for PC games running on Android. There’s no shortage of PC gaming emulators on Android, allowing you to run a variety of games on your phone, tablet, or handheld . However, you often need to install unofficial GPU drivers for the best performance and compatibility. Fortunately, it sounds like Qualcomm could bring improvements in this regard. Tech YouTuber Geekerwan reports that Qualcomm plans to improve support for PC game emulation on Android via its official GPU drivers. The YouTuber noted that they tried Cyberpunk 2077 and Black Myth: Wukong on a phone with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series chip. They reported that both games ran properly in DirectX12 mode using a translation layer.

title: Facing trouble with the Home Up Good Lock module? You’re not alone, and a fix is coming

body: TL;DR Home Up users may be unable to back up their settings if they have set custom folder label colors. Samsung is working on a fix and will roll it out in a future software update. For now, users can revert folder label colors to their default settings and create backups. As feature-packed as Samsung’s One UI already is, you can use Good Lock modules to get even more customization options for your phone. Modules like Home Up offer deep home screen customization, and you can even back up your settings and restore them later. However, there appears to be an issue with Home Up’s backup option that prevents users from restoring their settings. If you’re facing a similar issue on your Galaxy phone, you can rest easy knowing Samsung is already working on a fix. According to a post on the Samsung Community forums, the Home Up module’s backup feature doesn’t work properly if you’ve selected custom colors for folder labels. A Samsung Community moderator shared this information after a user reported that Home Up keeps deleting their backup file and telling them it’s “broken.”

title: Google Sheets now plays more nicely with your imported Excel spreadsheets
summary: Sheets also brings improvements for handling pivot tables.
body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users drag and drop rows or columns in pivot tables. It also maintains data hierarchy when moving rows or columns with nested child items. It now also preserves custom-sorted pivot tables when importing Excel spreadsheets. The last few months have been really great for Google Sheets users. Google has steadily rolled out new updates and features, introduced useful add-ons , and improved support for pivot tables . Now, it’s making it easier for users to manipulate pivot tables directly in Sheets. Google announced today that Sheets can now preserve custom sorting in pivot tables imported from Excel spreadsheets. Previously, Sheets reverted pivot tables to a standard alphanumeric sort order. However, it will now maintain any custom sort you’ve applied within Excel so you can easily move between the two apps. Exporting a Sheets file to an Excel spreadsheet also maintains the exact sorting order of your pivot tables.

title: Good Lock, bad lock screen: Weird bug messes with clock placement following One UI 9 update

Good Lock is supposed to give Galaxy owners more control over how One UI looks, but one Galaxy S26 Ultra user has found their carefully arranged lock screen doing its own thing after updating to One UI 9.
